short: Halving EMG electrodes costs synthesis the same ~35% relative WER known from recognition; initialization helps, channel dropout does not, and a weak unrepeated baseline undercuts the ranking.
position: The paper [1] changes sensing (M05, exhaustive 4-of-8 search) and training (M03, full-model initialization plus channel dropout); both are standard, and evaluation (M12) is behind. Its 8 → 4 cost, +35% relative, repeats EMG recognition (+32% [2], +36% [3]), and exhaustive EMG subset search exists [4]: synthesis confirms a known cost. Initialization helps at 4–6 electrodes; channel dropout does not (p=0 is best at 6 and 4), yet the introduction and conclusion credit it. The main confound is an unrepeated ~35% baseline, 8–10 points worse than the same lab's later reports [5], [6]: it inflates the absolute cost and leaves the 2.4-point top-10 spread inside seed noise. Virtual deletion cannot support device guidance.
